User Management now has three pages under it that overlap: this one, Accounts and Roles and Multiuser. A proposed division, with the two contradictions to settle; resolve with no reply to take it and I apply it (this page's Authorization section moves to Accounts and Roles, the references follow), or reply with changes.

**User Management** keeps the model (a person is the principal, an LLM is never a user, Scope decides, a token is the credential), the registry, the Users folder and user pages, tokens, runs as the presser, the Admin, the migration and the steps.

**Accounts and Roles** takes the account types (Administrator, User) and the project roles (Owner, Member, Service, Watcher), replacing this page's Authorization section, and defines Service: the account an external system or an agent acts under when it is not a person's token, writes within its role, presses no task, and is given a task-specific tool set when a task runs it.

**Multiuser** takes the rules with many parties: who resolves, who a thread waits on, who applies, the State by Owners, runs at any time (formalized today).

The two contradictions:

1. **Tasks per project or per server.** LLM Tasks says per server, with a project hiding some; Accounts and Roles says an Owner defines tasks for a project. Recommendation: per server, with hiding, as LLM Tasks decided; a project-defined task is a later step when a project needs one no other has.
2. **Members and tasks.** Accounts and Roles says a Member uses any task; LLM Tasks says what a role may press follows from the task's writes level, which gives a Member every task today anyway. Recommendation: keep the writes rule as the law and let Accounts and Roles state its result for each role, so a future task is governed by its record.

1. Tasks are defined per Server and enabled per Project.
2. Im not sure I understand what you are asking here.

Understood on 1: tasks are defined per server and enabled per project. That wording is now in LLM Tasks (revision 17), and Accounts and Roles will say it the same way when the division is applied.

On 2, put more plainly. Accounts and Roles says of a Member: "can use any LLM Task". LLM Tasks says which tasks a role may press is read from each task's Writes level: none for every role, consensus or files for Owners and Members. Both give a Member every task today, so there is no disagreement now. The question is which sentence is the rule when a new task appears, say one with Writes files that a team wants kept from Members. If the Writes level is the rule, the task's record decides and nothing else changes. If "any task" is the rule, roles would need a task list of their own. My recommendation is the Writes level as the rule, with Accounts and Roles stating what it comes to for each role today.

The division itself (this page keeps the model, registry, tokens, runs, Admin and migration; Accounts and Roles takes the account types and roles, this page's Authorization section moving there, and defines Service; Multiuser keeps the rules) stands as proposed. Resolve this thread with no reply to take the division and the recommendation on 2, and I move the section; reply if either should differ.

The rules run over speakers, keyed "<Service> by <By>" ("Claude-CLI by user"), plain By with no service. - The page: `State.BylineOf( record )` and a `byline` filter in app.js; the thread transcript, the revisions, the waiting list, a subplan's seed and the run rows show bylines; the Settings popup has an Owner row (Name read-only, Shown as) where the participants were; the LLM page says a connection's runs post as "<name> by <owner>"; the run buttons no longer ask about an llm role; the LLM Instructions popup's blurb.

**Checked**

**Decided during the build**

- A resolved thread waits on every speaker but the owner account, as it waited on the llm role: the LLMs and services apply, the owner may.
- The account asking is always among a plan's speakers, so an agent session sees what waits on it before it has spoken anywhere in the plan (the design said seen-in-threads; this keeps today's loop for a fresh session).
- With no LLM connection and nothing seen, a thread the owner opens waits on nobody; a connection or a session's first post fills the list. The "Waiting on …" filters list the owner and the connections.
- Everyone sees a connection's whole record (there is no token in it any more) and may start a run, since every request is the owner until Step 3.
- A run token is named after the task; the run record and its row show "<connection> by <owner>".
- The cube4 deploy file's LlmToken goes unused once cube4 is redeployed; the agent session there sends the header instead. This session's own helper switches to the header once this server is restarted on the new code.

**Design for Step 3, Users and roles.** Each point is a decision with my recommendation written out; resolving with no reply takes them all and I build. The step is large, so I build it in two checkpoints (the accounts, tokens and the API's role checks first; the Users folders and pages second) and post one build log at the end.

1. **The registry is one file on every server.** `<config>/Users.json` holds `{ Users: [ { Id (usr-…), Type: owner | user | service, Login, Display, Email, Clerk (the Clerk user id, null until sign-in), Tokens: [ { Name, Hash, Created, LastUsed } ], Created } ] }`. A Local or trusted-network server keeps it too, with the owner's record alone (Login the settings' Owner Name, Display its Display), made at the first start; so the tokens, the user page and the activity history are one code on every scope, and the plan's "no registry on Local" means no users besides the owner, not no file. Tokens are kept as a sha256 of the value, the value shown once when minted. *I recommend this: one shape everywhere, and the owner's own tokens on Local (Create token on the owner's page, so a thread can read "Claude Code by user") come for free.*

2. **Who a request is, until sign-in.** A bare request is the owner on a Local or trusted-network server, as now; on a Public server with a Clerk section it stays the owner too until Step 4 brings the session (said plainly in the Settings popup's trust line). A Bearer token is a run token (as now), else a user token matched by hash to a record, the request being that account with the token's name as Token and its LastUsed written; else 401. The byline reads "<Service> by <Login>". *I recommend this: Step 3 makes it possible to be someone other than the owner through a token, which is what the role checks need to be tested against, without waiting for Clerk.*

3. **Accounts before Clerk.** The Administrator (the owner on Local and on a trusted network; on a Public server with Clerk, the account whose Email is the Clerk section's AdminEmail, the owner meanwhile) makes accounts on the server-level Users folder: New user (email, login, display; a record Clerk completes at the person's first sign-in by matching the email, Step 4) and New Service account (a name; no email). The Administrator edits a login or display, deletes an account (out of every role folder, its tokens gone) and mints a Service account's tokens; a user edits their own display and mints and revokes their own tokens. *I recommend New user now rather than waiting for Clerk: it is the bridge that lets a Member and a Watcher exist on cube4 before sign-in, and the record is the same one Clerk will fill.*

4. **The role folders are the project's record.** project.json gets `Roles: { Owners, Members, Service, Watchers }`, each a list of account ids, an account in one at most, written through PUT /api/projects/:pid/roles by an Owner of the project or the Administrator. The page shows a fixed **Users** folder after the Context folder in every project, holding exactly the four, never renamed, moved or deleted; an account is dragged into one from the server-level Users folder, between them to change role, and out (Remove in its menu) to lose access; the folder shows each account's display name. The owner of a Local or trusted-network server needs no folder: the owner account passes every check. *I recommend this; the drag reuses the tree's drag code, and Remove in the menu covers what a drag out would.*

5. **The API checks every route against the role, in one place.** `src/Roles.js` names the actions (read, write, resolve, state, manage, roles, admin, press) and what each role allows, as Accounts and Roles says: Owners everything in the project; Members read, write, resolve the threads they started, press by Writes; Service read and write, press nothing; Watchers read and press Writes none; the Administrator admin (settings, connections, tasks, projects made and deleted, every user's page) and roles anywhere, plus a role folder like anyone's. A middleware after identify finds the project of the route (the project routes by id, the plan routes through the store's ProjectOf) and the account's role in it, and refuses with 403 and a plain reason ("a Watcher reads only", "no role in this project", "the Administrator's") before the route runs; the list routes (projects, plans, waiting, tasks) show a non-owner only the projects the account has a role in; a run's token carries the presser's role beside the task's Writes, so a run is allowed what the presser is, and a Service account starts no run. The owner account on Local and trusted network is everything, so nothing a bare request does today changes. *I recommend the table in one module with the middleware over it, rather than a check in each route: every route is covered the day it is written, and the tests read the table.*

6. **The Users folder and the user pages.** A server-level **Users** fold below the projects (beside the LLMs fold, `users-fold`), on every server: one row per account with its type; its menu New user, New Service account (the Administrator). A row opens a tab kind `u` (#/u/<account id>, `user-page`): the details (login, display, email, type, editable where allowed), the projects and the role in each, the tokens (Create token with a name, the value shown once with Copy, the list with each one's last use, Revoke), and the activity on the server (the threads, replies, revisions and state changes by that account, newest first, read from the data through GET /api/users/:id/activity). The owner's own page on Local is the same page. Every signed-in account sees the fold (names and display names); a page is the account's own or the Administrator's. *I recommend this.*

7. **The routes.** GET /api/users; POST /api/users { Type, Login, Display, Email? } (admin); GET /api/users/:id (self or admin, the tokens' names and last use, never a value); PUT /api/users/:id { Login?, Display? }; DELETE /api/users/:id (admin); POST /api/users/:id/tokens { Name } -> { Token, Name } once; DELETE /api/users/:id/tokens/:name; GET /api/users/:id/activity; PUT /api/projects/:pid/roles; GET /api/me answers the account (Id, Login, Display, Type, Admin) and its Roles by project. /instructions says a user token goes in Authorization: Bearer beside the service header. The desktop's connect screen is untouched in this step. *I recommend this.*

8. **Migration and the checks.** At the first start Users.json is written with the owner's record and each project.json gets empty Roles, with start-up lines; nothing else changes for the owner. Checks: `test/Users.test.js` (the records, hashing, mint and revoke, last use, the migration); `test/Roles.test.js` (the table, action by action); `test/Api.test.js` (accounts made by the Administrator, a token minted once and matched, revoked then 401; a Watcher reads a project, is refused every write with the reason, runs Explain and is refused Work; a Member writes, resolves a thread they started and not one the owner started, cannot set a state; an account with no role sees no project and is refused one; a Service account writes as a Member and starts no run; the owner's bare requests unchanged); `test/Ui.test.js` (the Users fold with the owner on Local, the owner's page with Create token and Revoke, the four role folders in a project, an account dragged into Watchers through the API shown there); the desktop smoke unchanged, the Member and Watcher smoke being Step 5. Docs: the README, `api.md`, `settings.md` (Users.json, Roles), `features.md`; the guide's pages on sharing a server and on roles are Step 5. *I recommend this.*
